title: Shopping & money
goal: Ask prices, bargain politely, buy clothes in the right size, and point out 'this one' and 'that one'.
intro: Tamil has a beautifully regular system of **demonstratives** built on three initial vowels: **இ-** 'this, here' (near me), **அ-** 'that, there' (away from me) and **எ-** 'which, where' (question). Once you know this, இது/அது/எது, இங்க/அங்க/எங்க, இப்போ/அப்போ/எப்போ all fall into place.

vocab.note: spoken: சீப் chīp; expensive = விலை அதிகம் / காஸ்ட்லி
spoken: விக்கு vikku; present விக்கிறாங்க vikkirānga
spoken: குடு kuḍu; past குடுத்தேன் kuḍuttēn

phrases.en: Do you have this in a bigger size?

grammar.title: The இ / அ / எ system: this, that, which
grammar.body:
Tamil demonstratives are built on three vowels: **இ-** near the speaker, **அ-** away from the speaker, **எ-** question.

இது *idu* this · அது *adu* that · எது *edu* which (one)?
இந்த *inda* this… · அந்த *anda* that… · எந்த *enda* which…?
இங்க *inga* here · அங்க *anga* there · எங்க *enga* where?
இப்போ *ippō* now · அப்போ *appō* then · எப்போ *eppō* when?
இப்படி *ippaḍi* like this · அப்படி *appaḍi* like that · எப்படி *eppaḍi* how?
இவ்வளவு *ivvaḷavu* this much · அவ்வளவு · எவ்வளவு how much?
இவரு / அவரு — this / that person (respectful)

**இது/அது** stand alone ('this one'); **இந்த/அந்த** go before a noun ('this shirt'). After இந்த/அந்த a following hard consonant is doubled in writing: அந்தச் சட்டை.

examples.en: I want this one, not that one.
Which shop did you buy it from?
I don't have that much money.

grammar.title: The object: accusative -ஐ (spoken -அ)
grammar.body:
When a **specific, definite** thing is the object of a verb, it takes the accusative **-ஐ** *-ai* (spoken often **-அ** *-a*): அந்தச் சட்டையைக் காட்டுங்க 'show me that shirt'. Indefinite or generic objects usually take no ending: நான் சட்டை வாங்கணும் 'I need to buy a shirt'.

Pronouns: என்னை / என்ன *ennai* 'me', உங்களை / உங்கள *ungaḷai* 'you', அவரை 'him/her', இதை / இத 'this', அதை / அத 'that'. Nouns use the oblique stem: வீடு → வீட்டை, மரம் → மரத்தை.

The emphatic **-ஏ** *-ē* means 'this very one, the same': இதையே 'this very one'.

examples.en: Where did you buy that sari?

dialogue.title: Bargaining for a shirt
dialogue.setting: Tom shops for a shirt at a street stall on Ranganathan Street.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Come in, sir! What do you need?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Show me that blue shirt, please.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.native: இதுவா? சூப்பர் காட்டன் சார். என்ன சைஸ்?
lines.roman: iduvā? sūppar kāṭṭan sār. enna sais?
lines.en: This one? Superb cotton, sir. What size?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: அறுநூறா? ரொம்ப அதிகம். முன்னூறு ரூபா தர்றேன்.
lines.roman: arunūrā? romba adigam. munnūru rūbā tarrēn.
lines.en: Six hundred? That's a lot. I'll give three hundred.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Oh sir, that won't work! Give me five hundred.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: OK sir, for you, four hundred and fifty.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: OK, I'll take this one. Can I pay by GPay?

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Go ahead, sir. Thanks, come again!

culture: Bargaining is expected at street stalls and markets but not in fixed-price shops, supermarkets or malls. Stay friendly and smiling — it's a social game, not a fight. Digital payments (UPI apps like GPay and PhonePe) are now used everywhere, even at tiny tea stalls. Tamil Nadu is famous for Kanchipuram silk saris (காஞ்சிப் பட்டு), the most prized wedding saris.
